_comment: Golden ambiguous-vs-unknown attribution cases (TOG-5849, prompt-quality slice of TOG-5681). Each case drives the REAL code in src/core/inviteTracker.ts - inviteGrowth + attributeJoins for kind=window, InviteTracker.attribute for kind=legacy-attribute - and the eval scores the fixture split: ambiguous cases must come back ambiguous, unknown cases unknown, and placed per-code splits must NOT read as ambiguous. See docs/FUNNEL_ATTRIBUTION_EVAL.md for how to add a case.

cases.title: Join while the bot was down reads unknown, never a guess
cases.why: Discord replays the member on reconnect but the invite delta is lost (EVENTS.md limit 3). The honest answer is unknown.

cases.title: Several offline joins are all unknown
cases.why: Nothing moved, so there is no code to name - not one guess per member, unknown per member.

cases.title: No movement with a vanity URL is vanity, not unknown
cases.why: Control for the unknown boundary: 'no code moved' alone does not mean unknown - the vanity URL is the probable path.

cases.title: Two codes moved but the arithmetic does not close: ambiguous
cases.why: Counters say 3 arrivals, the member list gained 2 - somebody joined and left inside the window. Any per-code split would be a guess printed as a number.

cases.title: Three codes moved without closing: one ambiguous string, not three guesses
cases.why: The failure mode this guards: splitting 3 members across a+2/b+1/c+1 when only 3 arrived. The codes join with + in sorted order.

cases.title: Two codes moved and the arithmetic closes: per-code counts, NOT ambiguous
cases.why: The TOG-5681 distinction. A +2 / B +1 with 3 arrivals is fully determined in aggregate - quoting it as ambiguous would throw away the campaign's per-code join counts.

cases.title: One code moved and the count closes: the only exact case
cases.why: Exactly one code gained exactly the arrivals observed. This - and only this - is proof a member came through that code.

cases.title: One code moved but two arrived: best guess, not proof
cases.why: Behaviour is unchanged - the code is still stamped on both - but exact stays false: one of the two did not come through it.

cases.title: A code created inside the window still claims its uses on the best-guess path
cases.why: The newest invite is usually the one a growth push is handing out. Fresh has +3 against 1 arrival: single code, no close, so best guess - but the code is named, not dropped.

cases.title: A reset code cannot cancel a real rise out of exactness
cases.why: Deleted-and-recreated codes reset to zero. Unclamped, the -9 would swallow real's +1 and this arrival would read unknown. Clamped, it is the ordinary exact case.

cases.title: Counters moved but nobody arrived: no attributions at all
cases.why: Uses can move without joins (bot restarts, recounts). A window with no new members emits nothing, whatever the counters did.

cases.title: Seven listing codes in one window keep their own counts
cases.why: The campaign shape: before the multi-code split this whole window recorded as one ambiguous:a+b+c+... string and launches had to be staggered to get readable numbers.

cases.title: Legacy path: two codes grew in one instant is ambiguous
cases.why: The live-bot single-join path (InviteTracker.attribute) has no magnitudes to split - two growers is genuinely unknowable and stays ambiguous:a+b.

cases.title: Legacy path: nothing grew and no vanity URL is unknown
cases.why: Discovery, or a code created while the bot was offline. Reported as itself, never folded into a real code.

cases.title: Legacy path: nothing grew with a vanity URL is vanity
cases.why: Control mirroring the window vanity case on the legacy path.

cases.title: Legacy path: exactly one code grew names that code
cases.why: The ordinary live-bot case. Exactness is not recorded on this path - that flag belongs to the windowed attributeJoins path.
